title.zh: 卷一百四十六 列傳第七十一 二李
title.raw: 卷一百四十六 列傳第七十一 二李 Volume 146 Biographies 71: Two Li's

sentences.zh: 李棲筠，字貞一，世為趙人。

translations.literal: Li Qiyun, courtesy name Zhenyi, was for generations a man of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qiyun, whose courtesy name was Zhenyi, came from a Zhao family of long standing.

sentences.zh: 幼孤。

translations.literal: Orphaned in youth.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his parents while still young.

sentences.zh: 有遠度，莊重寡言，體貌軒特。

translations.literal: He had far-reaching capacity, was solemn and sparing of speech, and his physique was lofty and striking.
translations.idiomatic: He possessed breadth of vision, was grave and reticent, and cut an imposing figure.

sentences.zh: 喜書，多所能曉，為文章，勁迅有體要。

translations.literal: He loved books, understood many fields, and in composing essays his style was vigorous and swift with structural essentials.
translations.idiomatic: A devoted reader, he was versed in many subjects; his prose was forceful and swift yet disciplined in form.

sentences.zh: 不妄交遊。

translations.literal: He did not associate casually.
translations.idiomatic: He made no friendships lightly.

sentences.zh: 族子華每稱有王佐才，士多慕向。

translations.literal: His kinsman Li Hua often said he had the talent of a chief minister's aide, and scholars mostly admired and turned toward him.
translations.idiomatic: His clansman Li Hua repeatedly praised him as having the makings of a statesman, and men of letters flocked to his side.

sentences.zh: 始，居汲共城山下，華固請舉進士，俄擢高第。

translations.literal: At first he lived at the foot of Gongcheng Mountain in Ji; Hua repeatedly urged him to enter the jinshi examination, and before long he won a top placement.
translations.idiomatic: He first lived below Gongcheng Mountain in Ji; Li Hua kept pressing him to sit for the jinshi, and he soon passed with a high rank.

sentences.zh: 調冠氏主簿，太守李峴視若布衣交。

translations.literal: He was appointed recorder of Guanshi; the prefect Li Xian treated him as a friend in plain dress.
translations.idiomatic: Assigned as recorder of Guanshi, he was received by Prefect Li Xian as an intimate equal, without regard to rank.

sentences.zh: 遷安西封常清節度府判官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be a staff judge in Feng Changqing's Anxi military commissioner's office.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to serve as a staff judge under Feng Changqing, military commissioner of Anxi.

sentences.zh: 常清被召，表攝監察御史，為行軍司馬。

translations.literal: When Changqing was summoned, [Qiyun] memorialized to have him act as investigating censor and made him campaign staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Changqing was recalled to court, Qiyun memorialized to have him act as investigating censor and appointed him campaign staff officer.

sentences.zh: 肅宗駐靈武，發安西兵，棲筠料精卒七千赴難，擢殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong halted at Lingwu and mobilized Anxi troops, Qiyun mustered seven thousand picked soldiers to go to the rescue and was promoted to attendant censor within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: As Emperor Suzong held at Lingwu and called up the Anxi army, Qiyun raised seven thousand elite troops for the emergency and was promoted to palace attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 李峴為大夫，以三司按群臣陷賊者，表棲筠為詳理判官。

translations.literal: When Li Xian became grandee and used the three bureaus to investigate officials who had fallen to the rebels, he memorialized to appoint Qiyun as detailed adjudication judge.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xian served as grand censor and used the three bureaus to examine officials who had submitted to the rebels, he recommended Qiyun as judge of detailed review.

sentences.zh: 推原其人所以脅汙者，輕重以情，悉心助峴，故峴愛恕之，譽一旦出呂諲、崔器上。

translations.literal: He traced how each person had been coerced into defilement, weighing severity and leniency according to circumstance, and assisted Xian with full devotion; hence Xian favored and forgave him, and his reputation one morning rose above Lü Yin and Cui Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He investigated how each man had been forced into complicity, adjusting penalties to the facts, and gave Xian his unstinting help; Xian cherished and excused him, and overnight his fame eclipsed that of Lü Yin and Cui Qi.

sentences.zh: 三遷吏部員外郎，判南曹。

translations.literal: After three promotions he became vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel and judged the southern bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted three times, he became vice minister of Personnel with charge of the southern bureau.

sentences.zh: 時大盜後，選簿亡舛，多偽冒，棲筠判析有條，吏氣奪，號神明。

translations.literal: At the time, after the great rebellion, appointment registers were lost and confused and many impostors appeared; Qiyun's rulings were orderly, clerks lost their arrogance, and he was called divine in judgment.
translations.idiomatic: In the aftermath of the great rebellion the appointment rolls were chaotic and fraud rampant; Qiyun's decisions were lucid and systematic, the clerks were cowed, and men called his judgment uncanny.

sentences.zh: 遷山南防禦觀察使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be defense and observation commissioner of Shannan.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed defense and observation commissioner of Shannan.

sentences.zh: 會峴去相，棲筠坐所善，除太子中允，眾不直，改河南令。

translations.literal: When Xian left the chancellorship, Qiyun was implicated through his friendship and appointed crown prince attendant, which the public deemed unjust; he was changed to magistrate of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: When Xian left the premiership, Qiyun was punished for their association and made crown prince attendant—a posting the public rejected as unfair—then reassigned as magistrate of Henan.

sentences.zh: 李光弼守河陽，高其才，引為行軍司馬，兼糧料使。

translations.literal: Li Guangbi held Heyang, valued his talent, and brought him in as campaign staff officer, also making him grain commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi, holding Heyang, admired his ability and took him on as campaign staff officer while also entrusting him with grain supply.

sentences.zh: 改絳州刺史，擢累給事中。

translations.literal: He was changed to prefect of Jiangzhou and promoted in succession to palace remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: He became prefect of Jiangzhou and was then promoted step by step to palace remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 是時，楊綰以進士不鄉舉，但試辭賦浮文，非取士之實，請置五經、秀才科。

translations.literal: At that time Yang Wan argued that jinshi candidates were not examined through local recommendation but only tested on florid rhapsodies and floating essays, which was not the substance of selecting talent, and requested establishing the Five Classics and Xiucai examinations.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yang Wan argued that the jinshi degree no longer rested on local nomination but on flashy literary exercises—a poor test of real ability—and urged new examinations in the Five Classics and the Xiucai category.

sentences.zh: 詔群臣議，棲筠與賈至、李廙以綰所言為是。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the ministers to discuss it; Qiyun, together with Jia Zhi and Li Yi, held that Wan's words were correct.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered discussion among the ministers; Qiyun, Jia Zhi, and Li Yi agreed with Wan.

sentences.zh: 進工部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was advanced to vice minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 關中舊仰鄭、白二渠溉田，而豪戚壅上遊取硙利，且百所，奪農用十七。

translations.literal: In Guanzhong the fields had long relied on the Zheng and Bai canals for irrigation, but powerful kin dammed the upper reaches for mill profits, nearly a hundred sites, seizing seven-tenths of the water for farming.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong had long depended on the Zheng and Bai canals to water its fields, yet powerful families blocked the upper reaches for milling profit—nearly a hundred such obstructions—depriving the farms of seven parts in ten of their water.

sentences.zh: 棲筠請皆徹毀，歲得租二百萬，民賴其入，魁然有宰相望。

translations.literal: Qiyun requested that all be torn down; each year two million in rent was gained, the people relied on the revenue, and he stood out with the look of a future chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyun petitioned to have them all demolished; annual grain rents rose by two million, the people prospered from the yield, and he loomed as a man marked for the highest office.

sentences.zh: 元載忌之，出為常州刺史。

translations.literal: Yuan Zai resented him and sent him out as prefect of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zai, jealous of him, had him posted out as prefect of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 歲仍旱，編人死徙踵路，棲筠為浚渠，廝江流灌田，遂大稔。

translations.literal: The year was still drought-stricken; registered households died and migrated along the roads in succession; Qiyun dug canals, channeled the river to irrigate fields, and thereupon a great harvest.
translations.idiomatic: Drought persisted; refugees and corpses lined the roads; Qiyun dredged canals and directed the river to the fields, and the district enjoyed a bumper harvest.

sentences.zh: 宿賊張度保陽羨西山，累年吏討不克，至是發卒捕斬，支黨皆盡，裏無吠狗。

translations.literal: The long-standing bandit Zhang Du held Yangxian's western hills; for years officials could not subdue him; now troops were sent to capture and behead him, his branches were all extinguished, and in the hamlets no dog barked.
translations.idiomatic: The veteran outlaw Zhang Du had held the western hills of Yangxian for years beyond official reach; Qiyun now sent soldiers who captured and executed him, rooted out his network, and left the countryside so quiet that no dog barked.

sentences.zh: 乃大起學校，堂上畫《孝友傳》示諸生，為鄉飲酒禮，登歌降飲，人人知勸。

translations.literal: He then greatly raised schools, painted the Record of Filial Piety and Fraternity in the hall to show the students, performed the district drinking ceremony with ascending song and descending drink, and everyone knew encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: He founded schools on a large scale, hung the Record of Filial Piety and Brotherhood in the hall for his pupils, and held village drinking rites with solemn song and shared cups until custom itself became instruction.

sentences.zh: 以治行進銀青光祿大夫，封贊皇縣子，賜一子官。

translations.literal: For his governance he was advanced to Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, enfeoffed as Viscount of Zanhuang, and one son was granted an office.
translations.idiomatic: On the strength of his administration he was promoted to Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, created Viscount of Zanhuang, and granted an office for one son.

sentences.zh: 人為刻石頌德。

translations.literal: The people had stone carved to praise his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The people set up stone inscriptions to praise his virtue.

sentences.zh: 蘇州豪士方清因歲兇，誘流殍為盜，積數萬，依黟、歙間，阻山自防，東南厭苦。

translations.literal: The powerful man of Suzhou Fang Qing, because of famine years, enticed wandering starvelings into banditry, amassed tens of thousands, relied on the region between Yi and She, blocked the mountains to defend themselves, and the southeast was wearied and afflicted.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Qing, a Suzhou magnate, exploited famine years to recruit starving refugees into a band of tens of thousands entrenched between Yi and She; the southeast groaned under their depredations.

sentences.zh: 詔李光弼分兵討平之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Li Guangbi to divide troops and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered Li Guangbi to detach forces and suppress them.

sentences.zh: 會平盧行軍司馬許杲恃功，擅留上元，有窺江、吳意，朝廷以創殘，重起兵，即拜棲筠浙西都團練觀察使圖之。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the Pinglu campaign staff officer Xu Gao relied on merit, detained himself at Shangyuan without leave, and had designs on Jiang and Wu; the court, because the realm was still wounded, dreaded raising troops again and at once appointed Qiyun regional training and observation commissioner of Zhexi to deal with him.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Xu Gao, campaign staff officer of Pinglu, abused his merits by lingering at Shangyuan with an eye on the lower Yangzi; the court, loath to mobilize again while the realm was still bleeding, appointed Qiyun regional commissioner of Zhexi to counter him.

sentences.zh: 棲筠至，張設武備，遣辯士厚賫金幣抵杲軍賞勞，使士歆愛，奪其謀。

translations.literal: When Qiyun arrived he displayed military preparations, sent eloquent men with generous gifts of gold and coin to Gao's army to reward and comfort them, made the soldiers delighted and attached, and seized away his schemes.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival Qiyun arrayed his forces, sent persuasive envoys laden with gold to Gao's camp to reward the troops, won their hearts, and undermined his designs.

sentences.zh: 杲懼，悉眾度江，掠楚、泗而潰。

translations.literal: Gao was afraid, led all his forces across the river, plundered Chu and Si, and broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Gao, alarmed, marched his whole force south of the river, ravaged Chu and Si, and collapsed in flight.

sentences.zh: 以功進兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: For merit he was advanced and concurrently made censor grandee.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he was promoted and also made censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 則又增學廬，表宿儒河南褚沖、吳何員等，超拜學官為之師，身執經問義，遠邇趨慕，至徒數百人。

translations.literal: He then again increased school buildings, memorialized for the veteran scholars Chu Chong of Henan, He Yuan of Wu, and others, promoted them beyond rule as school officials to be his teachers, personally held the classics and asked about meaning; near and far rushed in admiration, reaching several hundred disciples.
translations.idiomatic: He expanded the schools further, recommended venerable scholars such as Chu Chong of Henan and He Yuan of Wu, elevated them directly as masters, lectured on the classics himself, and drew hundreds of students from far and near.

sentences.zh: 又奏部豪姓多徙貫京兆、河南，規脫徭科，請量產出賦，以杜奸謀。

translations.literal: He also memorialized that powerful surnames in the prefecture mostly moved their registration to Jingzhao and Henan to scheme escape from corvée and tax categories, and requested assessing output for taxation to block crafty designs.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported that great clans were shifting household registration to the capital circuits to evade labor and tax levies, and urged assessments based on actual production to close such fraud.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 元載當國久，益恣橫，代宗不能堪，陰引剛鯁大臣自助，欲收綱權以黜載。

translations.literal: Yuan Zai had long held the state, grew ever more arbitrary, and Emperor Daizong could not bear it; he secretly drew in stern and upright great ministers to assist himself, wishing to gather the reins of power to dismiss Zai.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zai had dominated the government for years and grown ever more overbearing; Daizong, unable to endure it, quietly enlisted upright ministers to recover authority and remove him.

sentences.zh: 會御史大夫敬括卒，即召棲筠與河南尹張延賞，擇可為大夫者。

translations.literal: When censor grandee Jing Kuo died, he at once summoned Qiyun and Henan intendant Zhang Yanshang to choose who could be grandee.
translations.idiomatic: When Censor-in-Chief Jing Kuo died, the emperor summoned Qiyun and Zhang Yanshang, intendant of Henan, to choose a successor.

sentences.zh: 延賞先至，遂代括。

translations.literal: Yanshang arrived first and thereupon replaced Kuo.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshang reached the palace first and was appointed in Kuo's place.

sentences.zh: 會李少良、陸珽等上書劾載陰事，詔御史問狀，延賞稱疾，不敢鞫，少良、珽覆得罪死。

translations.literal: When Li Shaoliang, Lu Ting, and others memorialized impeaching Zai's secret affairs, an edict ordered the censorate to examine the case; Yanshang claimed illness and dared not try it; Shaoliang and Ting again offended and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shaoliang and Lu Ting impeached Zai's hidden crimes, the throne ordered the censorate to investigate; Yanshang pleaded illness and shrank from the trial; Shaoliang and Ting were condemned and executed.

sentences.zh: 帝殊失望，出延賞為淮南節度使，引拜棲筠為大夫。

translations.literal: The emperor was deeply disappointed, sent Yanshang out as military commissioner of Huainan, and summoned and appointed Qiyun as grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply disillusioned, the emperor posted Yanshang to Huainan as military commissioner and elevated Qiyun to censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 始，棲筠見帝，敷奏明辯，不阿附，帝心善之，故制麻自中以授，朝廷莫知也，中外竦眙。

translations.literal: At first when Qiyun saw the emperor he presented and memorialized clearly and discerningly, without flattery; the emperor's heart favored him, so the appointment edict was issued from within and given, the court did not know, and inside and outside were startled and wide-eyed.
translations.idiomatic: When Qiyun first audienceed the throne, his clear, unflinching memorials won the emperor's regard; the appointment edict was drafted in the inner palace before the court knew, and all were astonished.

sentences.zh: 棲筠素方挺，無所屈。

translations.literal: Qiyun had always been upright and unbending, yielding to nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyun had always been square and unyielding.

sentences.zh: 於是華原尉侯莫陳怤以優補長安尉，當參臺，棲筠物色其勞，怤色動，不能對，乃自言為徐浩、杜濟、薛邕所引，非真優也。

translations.literal: Thereupon Huayuan assistant Hou Mo Chen Fu was supplemented to Chang'an assistant through actor status; when he should attend the censorate, Qiyun scrutinized his labor records; Fu's color changed and he could not answer, then himself said he was introduced by Xu Hao, Du Ji, and Xue Yong, and was not a true actor.
translations.idiomatic: The Huayuan assistant Hou Mo Chen Fu had been slipped into a Chang'an post through claimed actor privilege; when he was to report to the censorate, Qiyun examined his service record; Fu blanched and confessed that Xu Hao, Du Ji, and Xue Yong had procured the appointment—he was no true actor at all.

sentences.zh: 始，浩罷嶺南節度使，以瑰貨數十萬餉載，而濟方為京兆，邕吏部侍郎，三人者，皆載所厚，棲筠並劾之。

translations.literal: Earlier Hao had left the post of Lingnan military commissioner and presented rare goods in the hundreds of thousands to Zai; Ji was then Jingzhao intendant and Yong vice minister of Personnel—the three were all men Zai favored—and Qiyun impeached them all.
translations.idiomatic: Hao had lately left the Lingnan commission with a gift of hundreds of thousands in precious goods for Zai; Ji was intendant of Jingzhao and Yong vice minister of Personnel—all three were Zai's protégés—and Qiyun impeached them together.

sentences.zh: 帝未決。

translations.literal: The emperor had not decided.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hesitated.

sentences.zh: 會月蝕，帝問其故，棲筠曰：「月蝕脩刑，今罔上行私者未得，天若以儆陛下邪？

translations.literal: When a lunar eclipse occurred the emperor asked its cause; Qiyun said: "A lunar eclipse means punishment should be carried out; now those who deceive the throne and pursue private ends have not been obtained—does Heaven perhaps warn Your Majesty?"
translations.idiomatic: During a lunar eclipse the emperor asked its meaning; Qiyun replied, "Eclipses warn that punishments must be enforced; men who deceive the throne still go free—is Heaven not admonishing Your Majesty?"

sentences.zh: 」繇是怤等皆坐貶。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Fu and the others all sat in demotion.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon Fu and his associates were all demoted.

sentences.zh: 故事，賜百官宴曲江，教坊倡顐雜侍，棲筠以任國風憲，獨不往，臺遂以為法。

translations.literal: By precedent the emperor granted the hundred officials a banquet at Qujiang with music-office singers and actors mixed in attendance; Qiyun, bearing national wind and discipline, alone did not go, and the censorate thereafter took it as rule.
translations.idiomatic: By custom the court feasted officials at Qujiang with entertainers in attendance; Qiyun, charged with national discipline, alone stayed away, and the censorate thereafter made that the standard.

sentences.zh: 帝比比欲召相，憚載輒止。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly wished to summon him as chancellor but feared Zai and always stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Again and again the emperor meant to make him chancellor, yet fear of Zai stayed his hand.

sentences.zh: 然有進用，皆密訪焉，多所補助。

translations.literal: Yet whenever there were promotions, he secretly consulted him, and in many matters was assisted.
translations.idiomatic: Still, on every important appointment he sought Qiyun's counsel in secret and leaned on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 棲筠見帝猗違不斷，亦內憂憤，卒，年五十八，自為墓誌。

translations.literal: Qiyun saw the emperor irresolute and undecided and also inwardly grieved and indignant; he died at fifty-eight, having written his own epitaph.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the emperor's vacillation, Qiyun brooded in private distress; he died at fifty-eight after composing his own epitaph.

sentences.zh: 贈吏部尚書，謚曰文獻。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made minister of Personnel and given the posthumous title Literary Contribution.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as minister of Personnel with the posthumous title Literary Contribution.

sentences.zh: 棲筠喜獎善，而樂人攻己短，為天下士歸重，不敢有所斥，稱贊皇公雲。

translations.literal: Qiyun delighted in rewarding goodness and rejoiced when others attacked his shortcomings; scholars under heaven turned to honor him, none daring to slight him, and called him Duke of Zanhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He delighted in praising merit and welcomed criticism of his faults; scholars everywhere deferred to him, and none spoke ill of the man they called Duke of Zanhuang.

sentences.zh: 子吉甫。

translations.literal: His son Jifu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Li Jifu.

sentences.zh: 吉甫字弘憲，以蔭補左司禦率府倉曹參軍。

translations.literal: Jifu, courtesy name Hongxian, entered through yin privilege as granary clerk of the Left Bureau of the Imperial Guard Rate Office.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu, courtesy name Hongxian, entered service by yin privilege as a clerk in the Left Imperial Guard granary office.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，為太常博士，年尚少，明練典故。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyuan he was made Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; though still young, he was clear and practiced in precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenyuan era he became an Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; though young, he was already expert in ritual precedent.

sentences.zh: 昭德皇后崩，自天寶後中宮虛，恤禮廢缺。

translations.literal: When Empress Zhaode died, since Tianbao the inner palace had been vacant and mourning rites were abandoned and lacking.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Zhaode died, the inner palace had stood empty since the Tianbao era and mourning observances had fallen into neglect.

sentences.zh: 吉甫草具其儀，德宗稱善。

translations.literal: Jifu drafted and completed its rites; Dezong praised them as good.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu drafted the full rites to the emperor's approval.

sentences.zh: 李泌、竇參器其才，厚遇之。

translations.literal: Li Mi and Dou Can valued his talent and treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi and Dou Can admired his talent and treated him generously.

sentences.zh: 陸贄疑有黨，出為明州長史。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi suspected he had a faction and sent him out as chief administrator of Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi, suspecting factional ties, posted him out as chief administrator of Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 贄之貶忠州，宰相欲害之，起吉甫為忠州刺史，使甘心焉。

translations.literal: When Zhi was demoted to Zhongzhou the chancellors wished to harm him and raised Jifu as prefect of Zhongzhou to make him vent his resentment there.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhi was banished to Zhongzhou the chancellors meant to destroy him and appointed Jifu prefect there, expecting him to settle old scores.

sentences.zh: 既至，置怨，與結歡，人益重其量，坐是不徙者六歲。

translations.literal: Once he arrived he set aside resentment and formed friendship with him; people increasingly respected his breadth, and for this reason he was not transferred for six years.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he put aside enmity and befriended Zhi; men admired his magnanimity all the more, and he remained in place six years without transfer.

sentences.zh: 改郴、饒二州。

translations.literal: He was changed to the two prefectures Chen and Rao.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Chen and Rao prefectures.

sentences.zh: 會前刺史繼死，咸言牙城有物怪，不敢居。

translations.literal: It happened that the previous prefects died in succession; all said the yamen city had strange creatures and dared not dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: Successive prefects had died in office, and everyone said the yamen was haunted; none would live there.

sentences.zh: 吉甫命菑除其署以視事，吏由是安。

translations.literal: Jifu ordered the overgrown removed from the offices to conduct affairs, and the clerks thereby were at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu had the compound cleared and took up residence; the staff were reassured.

sentences.zh: 誅破奸盜窟穴，治稱流聞。

translations.literal: He executed and broke the dens of treacherous bandits; his governance's fame spread abroad.
translations.idiomatic: He uprooted nests of banditry, and reports of his governance spread far.

sentences.zh: 憲宗立，以考功郎中召，知制誥。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong ascended he was summoned as director of the Bureau of Evaluations and made drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzong took the throne, Jifu was recalled as director of the Bureau of Evaluations and entrusted with drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 俄入翰林為學士，遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: Before long he entered the Hanlin as academician and was transferred to Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He soon entered the Hanlin Academy and was promoted to Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 劉闢拒命，帝意討之，未決。

translations.literal: Liu Pi refused orders; the emperor intended to attack him but had not decided.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Pi defied the throne; the emperor wished to campaign against him but had not decided.

sentences.zh: 吉甫獨請無置，宜絕朝貢以折奸謀。

translations.literal: Jifu alone requested no deployment and that court tribute be cut off to break treacherous designs.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu alone urged that no army be sent and that court tribute be cut off to frustrate his conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 時李錡在浙西，厚賂貴幸，請用韓滉故事領鹽鐵，又求宣、歙。

translations.literal: At that time Li Qi was in Zhexi, bribed the favored heavily, and requested using Han Huang's precedent to head salt and iron, also seeking Xuan and She.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi then held Zhexi, lavished gifts on the emperor's favorites, and asked—citing Han Huang's precedent—to control the salt and iron monopoly while also seeking Xuan and She prefectures.

sentences.zh: 問吉甫，對曰：「昔韋臯蓄財多，故劉闢因以構亂。

translations.literal: The emperor asked Jifu; he replied: "In the past Wei Gao amassed much wealth, and therefore Liu Pi was able to raise rebellion thereby."
translations.idiomatic: Asked for his view, Jifu replied, "Wei Gao once hoarded vast wealth, and Liu Pi used that wealth to raise rebellion."

sentences.zh: 李錡不臣有萌，若益以鹽鐵之饒、采石之險，是趣其反也。

translations.literal: Li Qi already had the sprout of disloyalty; if he were further given the richness of salt and iron and the peril of Caishi, that would hasten his revolt.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi already shows the seeds of disloyalty; to add the riches of the salt monopoly and the strategic choke point of Caishi would only hasten his revolt.

sentences.zh: 」帝寤，乃以李巽為鹽鐵使。

translations.literal: " The emperor awoke and thereupon made Li Xun salt and iron commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor took heed and appointed Li Xun salt and iron commissioner instead.

sentences.zh: 高崇文圍鹿頭未下，嚴礪請出并州兵，與崇文趨果、閬，以攻渝、合，吉甫以為非是，因言：「漢伐公孫述，晉伐李勢，宋伐譙縱，梁伐劉季連、蕭紀，凡五攻蜀，繇江道者四。

translations.literal: Gao Chongwen besieged Lutou but had not taken it; Yan Li requested sending out Bingzhou troops to join Chongwen in rushing toward Guo and Lang to attack Yu and He; Jifu thought this wrong and therefore said: "Han attacked Gongsun Shu, Jin attacked Li Shi, Song attacked Qiao Zong, Liang attacked Liu Jilian and Xiao Ji—in all five attacks on Shu, four went by the river route."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Chongwen had invested Lutou without success; Yan Li proposed marching Bingzhou troops with Chongwen toward Guo and Lang to strike Yu and He; Jifu objected, noting that of the five historical campaigns against Shu—from Han against Gongsun Shu to Liang against Liu Jilian and Xiao Ji—four had advanced along the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 且宣、洪、蘄、鄂強弩，號天下精兵，爭險地兵家所長，請起其兵搗三峽之虛，則賊勢必分，首尾不救，崇文懼舟師成功，人有鬥誌矣。

translations.literal: Moreover Xuan, Hong, Qi, and E have strong crossbows, called the finest troops under heaven; contesting perilous ground is what soldiers excel at—please raise their troops to strike the emptiness of the Three Gorges, then the rebels' force must divide, head and tail unable to rescue each other, and Chongwen, fearing the river army's success, will have men with fighting will.
translations.idiomatic: The circuits of Xuan, Hong, Qi, and E field the empire's finest crossbowmen, masters of difficult terrain; raise their forces to strike through the Three Gorges, he argued, and the rebels must split their strength; Chongwen, seeing the river fleet succeed, would fight with renewed zeal.

sentences.zh: 」帝從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor followed it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 礪復請大臣為節度，吉甫諫曰：「崇文功且成，而又命帥，不復盡力矣。

translations.literal: Li again requested a great minister as military commissioner; Jifu remonstrated: "Chongwen's merit is about to be achieved, and if again a commander is appointed, he will no longer exert full effort."
translations.idiomatic: Li again urged appointing a senior minister as commissioner; Jifu remonstrated, "Chongwen is on the verge of victory; name another commander over him and he will slacken."

sentences.zh: 」因請以西川授崇文，而屬礪東川，益資、簡六州，使兩川得以相制。

translations.literal: " He therefore requested giving Western Chuan to Chongwen while subordinating Li to Eastern Chuan, adding the six prefectures Zi, Zi, Jian, and the rest, so the two Chuan could restrain each other.
translations.idiomatic: " He proposed granting Western Chuan to Chongwen, placing Li over Eastern Chuan with six additional prefectures, so the two commands could check each other.

sentences.zh: 由是崇文悉力。

translations.literal: Thereby Chongwen exerted full effort.
translations.idiomatic: Chongwen therefore gave the campaign his all.

sentences.zh: 劉闢平，吉甫謀居多。

translations.literal: When Liu Pi was pacified, Jifu's stratagems were mostly responsible.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Pi was suppressed, Jifu's strategy had carried the day.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃遣使請尋盟，吉甫議：「德宗初，未得南詔，故與吐蕃盟。

translations.literal: Tibet sent envoys requesting to renew alliance; Jifu argued: "At the beginning of Dezong, Nan Zhao had not been obtained, therefore he allied with Tibet."
translations.idiomatic: Tibet sent envoys seeking to renew the alliance; Jifu argued, "Early in Dezong's reign, before Nan Zhao submitted, the court allied with Tibet."

sentences.zh: 自異牟尋歸國，吐蕃不敢犯塞，誠許盟，則南詔怨望，邊隙日生。

translations.literal: Since Yi Mouxun returned to the state Tibet dared not violate the passes; if alliance is truly granted, Nan Zhao will resent and look askance, and border quarrels will arise day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Since Yi Mouxun returned to the empire Tibet has not dared raid the frontier; grant them a new treaty now and Nan Zhao will turn resentful, with border friction growing daily.

sentences.zh: 」帝辭其使。

translations.literal: " The emperor declined their envoys.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor dismissed their envoys.

sentences.zh: 復請獻濱塞亭障南北數千里求盟，吉甫謀曰：「邊境荒岨，犬牙相吞，邊吏按圖覆視，且不能知。

translations.literal: They again requested presenting frontier forts and beacon towers north and south for several thousand li to seek alliance; Jifu strategized: "The borderlands are wild and rugged, interlocking like dog's teeth; border officials examine maps repeatedly and still cannot know."
translations.idiomatic: They again offered maps of frontier forts and beacon towers along thousands of li in exchange for peace; Jifu countered, "The borderlands are rugged and interlocking; frontier officers cannot verify such maps even when they study them."

sentences.zh: 今吐蕃綿山跨谷，以數番紙而圖千里，起靈武，著劍門，要險之地所亡二三百所，有得地之名，而實喪之，陛下將安用此？

translations.literal: Now Tibet spans mountains and valleys, using several sheets of paper to map a thousand li, from Lingwu to Jianmen; crucial perilous places lost number two or three hundred—there are names of gained territory but in fact territory is lost; how will Your Majesty use this?
translations.idiomatic: Now they span mountains and valleys on a few sheets of paper claiming a thousand li from Lingwu to Jianmen, erasing two or three hundred strategic posts in name while surrendering them in fact—of what use is such a map to Your Majesty?"

sentences.zh: 」帝乃詔謝贊普，不納。

translations.literal: " The emperor then edicted thanks to the tsenpo and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor then politely refused the Tibetan king.

sentences.zh: 張愔既得徐州，帝又欲以濠、泗二州還其軍，吉甫曰：「泗負淮，餉道所會，濠有渦口之險，前日授建封，幾失形勢。

translations.literal: When Zhang Yin had already obtained Xuzhou the emperor again wished to return the two prefectures Hao and Si to his army; Jifu said: "Si bears on the Huai, where supply routes meet; Hao has the peril of Wokou—in the past granting it to Jianfeng nearly lost the strategic posture."
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Yin secured Xuzhou the emperor again meant to restore Hao and Si to his command; Jifu warned, "Si commands the Huai and the junction of supply routes; Hao holds the strategic Wokou crossing—granting it to Jianfeng once nearly cost us the region."

sentences.zh: 今愔乃兩廊壯士所立，雖有善意，未能制其眾。

translations.literal: Now Yin was established by stalwart men of the two wings; though he has good intent, he cannot control his masses.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was installed by the garrison's own hard men; however well-intentioned he may be, he cannot control his troops.

sentences.zh: 又使得淮、渦，厄東南走集，憂未艾也。

translations.literal: If he again obtains control of the Huai and Wo, he will choke the southeast's routes of flight and gathering; the worry is not yet ended.
translations.idiomatic: Restore the Huai and Wo crossings and he will choke the southeast's lines of movement—the danger is not past.

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: " Thereupon it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " The plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 中書史滑渙素厚中人劉光琦，凡宰相議為光琦持異者，使渙請，常得如素，宦人傳詔，或不至中書，召渙於延英承旨，迎附群意，即為文書，宰相至有不及知者。

translations.literal: The Secretariat clerk Hua Huan had long been thick with the eunuch Liu Guangqi; whenever chancellors discussed holding a different view for Guangqi they had Huan request it and usually obtained it as before; eunuchs transmitted edicts and sometimes did not come to the Secretariat, summoning Huan at Yanying to receive the decree, courting and attaching to group opinions, immediately making documents—chancellors even had matters they did not know in time.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat clerk Hua Huan was intimate with the eunuch Liu Guangqi; whenever the chancellors opposed Liu's interests, Huan would intervene and usually prevail. Eunuchs sometimes bypassed the Secretariat entirely, summoning Huan to Yanying Hall to draft edicts to their liking—chancellors learned of policy only after the fact.

sentences.zh: 由是通四方賂謝，弟泳，官至刺史。

translations.literal: Thereby he connected bribes and thanks from the four directions; his younger brother Yong reached the office of prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Through him bribes flowed from every quarter; his brother Yong rose to prefect.

sentences.zh: 鄭餘慶當國，嘗一責怒，數日即罷去。

translations.literal: When Zheng Yuqing held the state he once rebuked him in anger; within several days he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Yuqing headed the government he rebuked Huan once; within days Huan was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 吉甫請間，劾其奸，帝使簿渙家，得貲數千萬，貶死雷州。

translations.literal: Jifu requested a private audience and impeached his treachery; the emperor had Huan's household audited and obtained assets of tens of millions; he was demoted and died at Leizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu sought a private audience and impeached him; auditors found tens of millions in his household; he was banished and died at Leizhou.

sentences.zh: 又建言：「州刺史不得擅見本道使，罷諸道歲終巡句以絕苛斂，命有司舉材堪縣令者，軍國大事以寶書易墨詔。

translations.literal: He also offered advice: "Prefects must not on their own see their circuit commissioners; abolish the circuits' year-end touring and collection to end harsh exactions; order the relevant offices to recommend talent fit to be county magistrates; for great military and state affairs use precious documents in place of ink edicts."
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed that prefects not meet circuit commissioners without authorization, that year-end circuit inspections be abolished to end extortion, that qualified magistrates be nominated by the ministries, and that critical military and state orders be issued on imperial treasure documents rather than informal ink edicts.

sentences.zh: 」由是帝愈倚信。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the emperor relied on him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: " From that time the emperor trusted him still more.

sentences.zh: 元和二年，杜黃裳罷宰相，乃擢吉甫中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanhe, Du Huangchang left the chancellorship, and Jifu was raised to vice director of the Secretariat and associate director of the Secretariat Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe year 2, after Du Huangchang left office, Jifu was elevated to vice director of the Secretariat and chancellor.

sentences.zh: 吉甫連蹇外遷十餘年，究知閭裏疾苦，常病方鎮強恣，至是為帝從容言：「使屬郡刺史得自為政，則風化可成。

translations.literal: Jifu had suffered successive setbacks and been transferred outward for more than ten years, thoroughly knowing the hardships of villages and lanes, and had long grieved that regional commands were strong and arbitrary; now he said to the emperor at ease: "If subordinate prefects are allowed to govern themselves, then transformation by instruction can be achieved."
translations.idiomatic: After more than a decade of setbacks in provincial posts he knew the people's hardships intimately and had long deplored the arrogance of the regional commands; he now told the emperor calmly, "Let subordinate prefects govern their own districts, and civilizing rule can take root."

sentences.zh: 」帝然之，出郎吏十餘人為刺史。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved, and sent out more than ten court gentlemen as prefects.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed and dispatched more than ten court officials as prefects.

sentences.zh: 自王叔文時選任猥冒，吉甫始簿其員，人得敘進，官無留才。

translations.literal: Since Wang Shuwen's time appointments had been vulgar and reckless; Jifu first registered their numbers, people could advance in order, and offices had no detained talent.
translations.idiomatic: Since Wang Shuwen's faction appointments had been chaotic; Jifu began keeping proper registers so men could advance by seniority and talent was no longer stranded in office.

sentences.zh: 又度錡必反，勸帝召之，使者三往，以病解，而多持金啗權貴，至為錡遊說者。

translations.literal: He also judged that Qi would surely rebel, urged the emperor to summon him, envoys went three times and he excused himself on grounds of illness, yet he carried much gold to bribe the powerful, even to the point of men lobbying for Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He also judged that Li Qi would rebel, urged the emperor to summon him to court; envoys went three times but Qi pleaded illness while bribing the powerful—even hiring lobbyists on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 吉甫曰：「錡，庸材，而所蓄乃亡命群盜，非有鬥誌，討之必克。

translations.literal: Jifu said: "Qi is mediocre talent, and what he gathers are desperate bandits without fighting will; attacking him will surely succeed."
translations.idiomatic: Jifu said, "Qi is a mediocrity surrounded by desperate outlaws without real fighting spirit; a campaign will surely prevail."

sentences.zh: 」帝意決。

translations.literal: " The emperor's mind was decided.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor's mind was made up.

sentences.zh: 復言：「昔徐州亂，嘗敗吳兵，江南畏之。

translations.literal: He again said: "In the past when Xuzhou rebelled it once defeated Wu troops, and Jiangnan feared it."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "When Xuzhou rebelled before it once defeated Wu armies, and the lower Yangzi still fears that memory."

sentences.zh: 若起其眾為先鋒，可以絕徐後患。

translations.literal: If their masses are raised as vanguard, Xuzhou's later trouble can be cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Raise those troops as the vanguard and the lingering threat from Xuzhou can be ended.

sentences.zh: 韓弘在汴州，多憚其威，誠詔弘子弟率兵為掎角，則賊不戰而潰。

translations.literal: Han Hong was at Bianzhou and greatly feared their might; truly order Hong's sons and younger brothers to lead troops as pincers, then the rebels will collapse without battle.
translations.idiomatic: Han Hong at Bianzhou fears their power; if he is ordered to flank them with his forces, the rebels will collapse without a fight.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: " The plan was adopted.

sentences.zh: 詔下，錡眾聞徐、梁兵興，果斬錡降。

translations.literal: When the edict descended, Qi's masses heard Xuzhou and Liang armies rising and indeed beheaded Qi and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict went out, Qi's followers heard that Xuzhou and Bianzhou armies were moving and beheaded Qi in surrender.

sentences.zh: 以功封贊皇縣侯，徙趙國公。

translations.literal: For merit he was enfeoffed Marquis of Zanhuang and transferred to Duke of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he was created Marquis of Zanhuang, then Duke of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 德宗以來，姑息蕃鎮，有終身不易地者。

translations.literal: Since Dezong there had been indulgence of frontier commands, with some not changing territory for life.
translations.idiomatic: Since Dezong's reign the court had indulged the regional commands, some holding the same territory for life.

sentences.zh: 吉甫為相歲餘，凡易三十六鎮，殿最分明。

translations.literal: Jifu as chancellor for more than a year changed thirty-six commands in all, with grades of merit and demerit clearly distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: In little more than a year as chancellor Jifu rotated thirty-six commands, with clear merit rankings for each.

sentences.zh: 裴均以尚書右僕射判度支，結黨傾執政。

translations.literal: Pei Jun held the right vice director of the Secretariat while judging the Revenue Bureau, formed a faction to overturn those in power.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Jun, as right vice director of the Secretariat with charge of the Revenue Bureau, built a faction to undermine the administration.

sentences.zh: 會皇甫湜等對策，指權強，用事者皆怒，帝亦不悅。

translations.literal: When Huangfu Shi and others answered policy questions, pointing at powerful men, those in charge were all angry and the emperor was also displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When Huangfu Shi and others answered the policy examination by denouncing the powerful, the power brokers were furious and the emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 均黨因宣言：「殆執政使然。

translations.literal: Jun's faction therefore proclaimed: "Perhaps the chancellors caused this."
translations.idiomatic: Jun's faction spread word that the chancellors were behind it.

sentences.zh: 」右拾遺獨孤郁、李正辭等陳述本末，帝乃解。

translations.literal: " Right remembrancer Dugu Yu, Li Zhengchen, and others stated the beginning and end, and the emperor then understood.
translations.idiomatic: " Right remembrancers Dugu Yu and Li Zhengchen explained what had happened, and the emperor was satisfied.

sentences.zh: 吉甫本善竇群、羊士諤、呂溫，薦群為御史中丞。

translations.literal: Jifu had originally been on good terms with Dou Qun, Yang Shie, and Lü Wen, and recommended Qun as censor vice director.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu had favored Dou Qun, Yang Shie, and Lü Wen and recommended Qun as vice director of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 群即奏士諤侍御史，溫知雜事。

translations.literal: Qun immediately memorialized Shie as attendant censor and Wen as controller of miscellaneous affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Qun at once appointed Shie attendant censor and Wen controller of miscellaneous affairs.

sentences.zh: 吉甫恨不先白，持之，久不決，群等銜之。

translations.literal: Jifu resented that he had not been informed first, held back, long did not decide, and Qun and the others harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu, angry that he had not been consulted, delayed approval for a long time, and Qun's circle bore a grudge.

sentences.zh: 俄而吉甫病，醫者夜宿其第，群捕醫者，劾吉甫交通術士。

translations.literal: Before long Jifu fell ill; a physician lodged overnight at his residence; Qun arrested the physician and impeached Jifu for associating with occultists.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Jifu fell ill and a physician stayed overnight at his house; Qun arrested the physician and impeached Jifu for consorting with occultists.

sentences.zh: 帝大駭，訊之無狀，群等皆貶。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly alarmed; inquiry found no basis; Qun and the others were all demoted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was alarmed, but investigation found no substance; Qun and his allies were all demoted.

sentences.zh: 而吉甫亦固乞免，因薦裴垍自代，乃以檢校兵部尚書、兼中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事，為淮南節度使。

translations.literal: Jifu also firmly begged to be relieved, and recommended Pei Ji to replace himself; thereupon with acting minister of War and concurrent vice director of the Secretariat and associate chancellor he became military commissioner of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu also insisted on resigning, recommended Pei Ji as his successor, and was posted to Huainan as military commissioner while Pei Ji took his chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 帝為御通化門祖道，賜御餌禁方。

translations.literal: The emperor personally saw him off at Tonghua Gate with a farewell feast and bestowed imperial diet and secret prescriptions.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw him off at Tonghua Gate with a farewell feast and bestowed imperial medicines and secret prescriptions.

sentences.zh: 居三歲，奏蠲逋租數百萬，築富人、固本二塘，溉田且萬頃。

translations.literal: After three years in office he memorialized remission of overdue rent of several millions, built the two ponds Furen and Guben, and irrigated nearly ten thousand qing of fields.
translations.idiomatic: In three years he secured remission of millions in overdue rents, built the Furen and Guben reservoirs, and irrigated nearly ten thousand qing of farmland.

sentences.zh: 漕渠庳下不能居水，乃築堤閼以防不足，泄有餘，名曰平津堰。

translations.literal: The transport canal was low and could not hold water; he therefore built dikes and sluices to guard against shortage and release surplus, named Pingjin Weir.
translations.idiomatic: The transport canal ran too low to hold water; he built dikes and sluices to store surplus flow and release it when needed—the Pingjin Weir.

sentences.zh: 江淮旱，浙東、西尤甚，有司不為請，吉甫白以時救恤，帝驚，馳遣使分道賑貸。

translations.literal: Jianghuai suffered drought, eastern and western Zhe especially severely; the relevant offices did not request relief; Jifu reported timely rescue and succor; the emperor was startled and swiftly sent envoys by separate routes to grant relief loans.
translations.idiomatic: Drought struck the Jianghuai region, worst in eastern and western Zhe; the ministries had not petitioned for relief; Jifu reported the crisis; the emperor was startled and dispatched envoys on separate routes to distribute aid.

sentences.zh: 吉甫雖居外，每朝廷得失輒以聞。

translations.literal: Although Jifu dwelt outside, whenever the court had gains or losses he immediately reported them.
translations.idiomatic: Though posted far from the capital, he kept the throne informed of every important development at court.

sentences.zh: 六年，裴垍病免，復以前官召吉甫還秉政。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Pei Ji resigned on illness; Jifu was again summoned with his former offices to return and hold government.
translations.idiomatic: In year six Pei Ji resigned through illness; Jifu was recalled to his former posts at the helm of government.

sentences.zh: 入對延英，凡五刻罷。

translations.literal: He entered audience at Yanying and after five quarter-hours was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He audienceed at Yanying Hall for five quarter-hours before the session ended.

sentences.zh: 帝尊任之，官而不名。

translations.literal: The emperor honored and entrusted him, addressing him by office and not by name.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor honored him so highly that he addressed him by title rather than by name.

sentences.zh: 吉甫疾吏員廣，繇漢至隋，未有多於今者，乃奏曰：「方今置吏不精，流品龐雜，存無事之官，食至重之稅，故生人日困，冗食日滋。

translations.literal: Jifu grieved that clerical posts were broad; from Han through Sui none had been more numerous than now; he memorialized: "At present appointment of officials is not refined, ranks and categories are bloated and mixed, idle offices without duties are kept, and they consume the heaviest taxes, therefore the living daily grow distressed and superfluous eaters daily increase."
translations.idiomatic: Jifu deplored the swollen bureaucracy—never since Han and Sui had there been so many officials—and memorialized: "Appointments are careless, ranks chaotic, idle posts abound, and they consume the heaviest taxes, so the people grow poorer daily while useless mouths multiply."

sentences.zh: 又國家自天寶以來，宿兵常八十餘萬，其去為商販、度為佛老、雜入科役者，率十五以上。

translations.literal: Moreover since Tianbao the state has constantly kept more than eight hundred thousand standing troops; of those who leave to become merchants, enter Buddhism or Daoism, or are mixed into corvée categories, on average more than fifteen in a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Since Tianbao the standing army has held over eight hundred thousand men, yet more than fifteen in a hundred slip away into trade, Buddhism, Daoism, or evasion of corvée.

sentences.zh: 天下常以勞苦之人三，奉坐待衣食之人七。

translations.literal: Under heaven there are habitually three laboring and toiling people for every seven who sit awaiting food and clothing.
translations.idiomatic: For every three who labor, seven merely wait to be fed.

sentences.zh: 而內外官仰奉稟者，無慮萬員，有職局重出，名異事離者甚眾，故財日寡而受祿多，官有限而調無數。

translations.literal: Yet inner and outer officials relying on state salaries are no fewer than ten thousand; many have duplicate bureaus reappearing, names differing and affairs separated; therefore wealth daily grows scarce while recipients of salary grow many, offices are limited but assignments are countless.
translations.idiomatic: Yet salaried officials inside and outside the capital number nearly ten thousand, with duplicated bureaus and overlapping duties everywhere—revenue shrinks while stipends swell, fixed posts multiply while assignments have no limit.

sentences.zh: 九流安得不雜？

translations.literal: How can the nine ranks not be mixed?
translations.idiomatic: How can ranks and duties not fall into chaos?

sentences.zh: 萬務安得不煩？

translations.literal: How can the ten thousand affairs not be vexed?
translations.idiomatic: How can government not become hopelessly burdensome?

sentences.zh: 漢初置郡不過六十，而文、景化幾三王，則郡少不必政紊，郡多不必事治。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han there were no more than sixty commanderies established, yet under Wen and Jing transformation nearly reached three kings—few commanderies does not necessarily mean disorder in government, many commanderies does not necessarily mean affairs well governed.
translations.idiomatic: Early Han had fewer than sixty commanderies, yet Wen and Jing nearly saw the realm split among three kings—fewer districts do not guarantee good order, nor do more districts guarantee effective rule.

sentences.zh: 今列州三百、縣千四百，以邑設州，以鄉分縣，費廣制輕，非致化之本。

translations.literal: Now there are three hundred listed prefectures and fourteen hundred counties, establishing prefectures from towns and dividing counties from townships—expense broad and control light, not the root of achieving transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Today there are three hundred prefectures and fourteen hundred counties—prefectures carved from mere towns, counties from mere townships—costly yet weak in control, not the foundation of good government.

sentences.zh: 願詔有司博議，州縣有可並並之，歲時入仕有可停停之，則吏寡易求，官少易治。

translations.literal: I wish an edict ordering the relevant offices to discuss broadly: where prefectures and counties can be merged, merge them; where yearly entry to office can be halted, halt it—then clerks will be few and easy to seek, offices few and easy to govern.
translations.idiomatic: I urge a broad review: merge redundant prefectures and counties, suspend unnecessary recruitment cycles—then fewer officials will be easier to find and easier to govern.

sentences.zh: 國家之制，官一品，奉三千，職田祿米大抵不過千石。

translations.literal: The state's system: rank one office, salary three thousand, duty fields and salary grain in general not exceeding one thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: By statute a first-rank official received three thousand in salary, with duty fields and grain stipends generally not exceeding one thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 大歷時，權臣月奉至九千緡者，州刺史無大小皆千緡，宰相常袞始為裁限，至李泌量閑劇稍增之，使相通濟。

translations.literal: In the Dali era powerful ministers' monthly salaries reached nine thousand strings; prefects large and small all had one thousand strings; Chancellor Chang Gun first set cut limits; by Li Mi's time busy and idle posts were measured and slightly increased to allow mutual aid.
translations.idiomatic: Under Dali, powerful ministers drew monthly salaries of nine thousand strings and every prefect one thousand; Chang Gun first imposed limits; Li Mi later adjusted pay by the demands of each post so offices could support one another.

sentences.zh: 然有名在職廢，奉存額去，閑劇之間，厚薄頓異，亦請一切商定。

translations.literal: Yet there are cases where the name remains but the duty is abolished, salary quota kept though the post is gone; between idle and busy posts thick and thin suddenly differ—I also request that all be fixed by agreement.
translations.idiomatic: Yet many hold titles without duties while drawing full pay, and stipends vary wildly between busy and idle posts—I ask that all salaries be standardized.

sentences.zh: 」乃詔給事中段平仲、中書舍人韋貫之、兵部侍郎許孟容、戶部侍郎李絳參閱蠲減，凡省冗官八百員，吏千四百員。

translations.literal: " An edict then ordered supervising secretary Duan Pingzhong, Secretariat drafter Wei Guanzhi, vice minister of War Xu Mengrong, and vice minister of Revenue Li Jiang to examine and reduce; in all superfluous offices were cut by eight hundred posts and clerks by fourteen hundred.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor ordered Duan Pingzhong, Wei Guanzhi, Xu Mengrong, and Li Jiang to review and cut redundancies—eight hundred superfluous posts and fourteen hundred clerks were eliminated.

sentences.zh: 又奏收都畿佛祠田、硙租入，以寬貧民。

translations.literal: He also memorialized to reclaim Buddhist temple fields and mill rents in the capital region for revenue to relieve the poor.
translations.idiomatic: He also petitioned to reclaim temple lands and mill revenues around the capital to ease the burden on the poor.

sentences.zh: 德宗時，義陽、義章二公主薨，詔起祠堂於墓百二十楹，費數萬計。

translations.literal: In Dezong's time the two princesses Yiyang and Yizhang died; an edict ordered raising ancestral halls at the tombs of one hundred twenty bays, costing tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Under Dezong, when Princesses Yiyang and Yizhang died, the court built ancestral halls of one hundred twenty bays at their tombs at a cost of tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 會永昌公主薨，有司以請，帝命減義陽之半。

translations.literal: When Princess Yongchang died the relevant offices requested [the same]; the emperor ordered half of Yiyang's scale.
translations.idiomatic: When Princess Yongchang died the ministries requested similar honors; the emperor ordered half the scale granted to Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 吉甫曰：「德宗一切之恩，不可為法。

translations.literal: Jifu said: "Dezong's indiscriminate favors cannot serve as precedent."
translations.idiomatic: Jifu said, "Dezong's indiscriminate largesse must not become precedent."

sentences.zh: 昔漢章帝欲起邑屋於親陵，東平王蒼以為不可。

translations.literal: In the past Emperor Zhang of Han wished to raise town houses at the imperial clan tombs; the Prince of Dongping, Cang, held it impossible.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhang of Han wished to build town houses at the imperial tombs, the Prince of Dongping, Liu Cang, declared it impermissible.

sentences.zh: 故非禮之舉，人君所慎。

translations.literal: Therefore unritual acts are what the ruler must be cautious of.
translations.idiomatic: Unorthodox observances are what a ruler must guard against.

sentences.zh: 請裁置墓戶，以充守奉。

translations.literal: I request trimming and setting tomb households to suffice for guarding and maintenance.
translations.idiomatic: I urge instead assigning tomb households sufficient to maintain the graves.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「吾固疑其冗，減之，今果然。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "I had long suspected it excessive; reduce it—now it is truly so."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "I had long suspected the expense excessive; reduce it—as you say, it proves so."

sentences.zh: 然不欲取編民，以官戶奉墳而已。

translations.literal: Yet I do not wish to take registered civilians; only official households to serve the tombs.
translations.idiomatic: But I will not draft commoners—official households alone shall maintain the tombs.

sentences.zh: 」吉甫再拜謝。

translations.literal: " Jifu bowed twice in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: " Jifu bowed in thanks.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「事不安者第言之，無謂朕不能行也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Whatever affairs are not sound, simply speak of them; do not think I cannot carry them out."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Speak freely whenever something troubles you; do not imagine I cannot act."

sentences.zh: 」十宅諸王既不出閤，諸女嫁不時，而選尚皆繇中人，厚為財謝乃得遣。

translations.literal: " The princes of the Ten Residences did not leave the inner quarters; the princesses were not married in season; selection of imperial sons-in-law all went through eunuchs, who received heavy gifts in thanks before dispatch was granted.
translations.idiomatic: " The princes of the Ten Residences never left the palace, princesses married late, and matches were brokered by eunuchs who demanded heavy bribes before consenting.

sentences.zh: 吉甫奏：「自古尚主必慎擇其人。

translations.literal: Jifu memorialized: "Since antiquity marrying a princess to a subject has required careful choice of the man."
translations.idiomatic: Jifu memorialized, "Since antiquity imperial marriages required the most careful selection of bridegrooms."

sentences.zh: 江左悉取名士，獨近世不然。

translations.literal: In the southeast they all took famous scholars; only in recent times is it not so.
translations.idiomatic: In the south they chose eminent scholars; only in recent times has that ceased.

sentences.zh: 」帝乃下詔皆封縣主，令有司取門閥者配焉。

translations.literal: " The emperor then issued an edict enfeoffing all as county princesses and ordering the relevant offices to take men of eminent gates and marry them.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor then enfeoffed them all as county princesses and ordered the ministries to match them with men of good family.

sentences.zh: 田季安疾甚，吉甫請任薛平為義成節度使，以重兵控邢、洺，因圖上河北險要所在，帝張於浴堂門壁，每議河北事，必指吉甫曰：「朕日按圖，信如卿料矣。

translations.literal: When Tian Ji'an was gravely ill, Jifu requested appointing Xue Ping as military commissioner of Yicheng, using heavy troops to control Xing and Ming; he also submitted a map of Hebei's strategic points; the emperor hung it on the Bath Hall gate wall; whenever Hebei affairs were discussed he would point to Jifu and say: "I daily consult this map—it is truly as you foresaw."
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Ji'an fell gravely ill, Jifu urged appointing Xue Ping commissioner of Yicheng with strong forces to hold Xing and Ming, and submitted a map of Hebei's strategic points; the emperor hung it on the Bath Hall gate; whenever Hebei was discussed he told Jifu, "I study this map daily—your foresight is proved."

sentences.zh: 」劉澭舊軍屯普潤，數暴掠近縣，吉甫奏還涇原，畿民賴之。

translations.literal: " Liu Yong's old army was stationed at Purun and repeatedly raided nearby counties; Jifu memorialized to return them to Jingyuan, and capital-region people relied on this.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Yong's old garrison at Purun had repeatedly raided neighboring counties; Jifu had them returned to Jingyuan, to the great relief of the capital region.

sentences.zh: 八年，回鶻引兵自西城、柳谷侵吐蕃，塞下傳言且入寇。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the Uyghurs led troops from Xicheng and Liugu to invade Tibet; along the frontier rumors spread that they would soon raid in.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight the Uyghurs marched through Xicheng and Liugu to attack Tibet, and frontier rumor said they would raid the border next.

sentences.zh: 吉甫曰：「回鶻能為我寇，當先絕和而後犯邊，今不足虞也。

translations.literal: Jifu said: "If the Uyghurs could raid us they would first break alliance and then violate the border; now they are not worth worrying over."
translations.idiomatic: Jifu said, "If the Uyghurs meant to raid us they would break the alliance first; there is no cause for alarm yet."

sentences.zh: 」因請起夏州至天德復驛候十一區，以通緩急；

translations.literal: " He therefore requested restoring eleven courier and watch districts from Xiazhou to Tiande to connect urgent and routine communications;
translations.idiomatic: " He urged restoring eleven courier and watch stations from Xiazhou to Tiande for emergency communications;

sentences.zh: 發夏州精騎五百屯經略故城，以護党項而已。

translations.literal: dispatch five hundred picked Xiazhou cavalry to garrison the old Jinglue city to protect the Tangut tribes only.
translations.idiomatic: and station five hundred elite Xiazhou horsemen at the old Jinglue fortress to protect the Tangut tribes.

sentences.zh: 既而果邊吏妄言。

translations.literal: Before long it proved to be frontier officials' false reports.
translations.idiomatic: The alarm proved to be a false report by frontier officials.

sentences.zh: 六胡州在靈武部中，開元時廢之，置宥州以處降戶，寓治經略軍，居中以制戎虜，北援天德，南接夏州。

translations.literal: The Six Hu Prefectures lay within Lingwu circuit; in Kaiyuan they were abolished and Youzhou was set to settle surrendered households, with administration lodged at the Jinglue army, centered to control barbarian enemies, aiding Tiande to the north and connecting Xiazhou to the south.
translations.idiomatic: The Six Hu prefectures lay within Lingwu; Kaiyuan abolished them and created Youzhou for surrendered tribes, administered from the Jinglue army to control the frontier, supporting Tiande in the north and Xiazhou in the south.

sentences.zh: 至德、寶應間，廢宥州，以軍遙隸靈武，道裏曠遠，故党項孤弱，虜數擾之。

translations.literal: Between Zhide and Baoying Youzhou was abolished and the army remotely subordinated to Lingwu; roads and li were vast and distant, therefore the Tangut were isolated and weak and the barbarians repeatedly harassed them.
translations.idiomatic: Between Zhide and Baoying Youzhou was abolished and the army placed under distant Lingwu control; the Tangut were isolated and barbarians raided them repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 吉甫始奏復宥州，乃治經略軍，以隸綏銀道，取鄜城神策屯兵九千實之。

translations.literal: Jifu first memorialized to restore Youzhou, then governed the Jinglue army, subordinating it to the Suiyin circuit, taking nine thousand Shence garrison troops from Fucheng to fill it.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu first restored Youzhou, reorganized the Jinglue army under the Suiyin circuit, and filled it with nine thousand Shence troops from Fucheng.

sentences.zh: 以江淮甲三十萬給太原、澤潞軍，增太原馬千匹。

translations.literal: Three hundred thousand suits of armor from Jianghuai were given to the Taiyuan and Zelu armies, and Taiyuan horses were increased by one thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Three hundred thousand suits of armor from Jianghuai were sent to Taiyuan and Zelu, and Taiyuan's horse herds were increased by one thousand.

sentences.zh: 由是戎備完輯。

translations.literal: Thereby frontier preparations were complete and in order.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier defenses were thereby brought into good order.

sentences.zh: 自蜀平，帝銳意欲取淮西。

translations.literal: Since Shu was pacified the emperor was keen in mind to take Huaixi.
translations.idiomatic: After the pacification of Shu the emperor was determined to seize Huaixi.

sentences.zh: 方吉甫在淮南，聞吳少陽立，上下攜泮，自請徙壽州，以天子命招懷之，反間以撓其黨，會討王承宗，未及用。

translations.literal: While Jifu was in Huainan he heard Wu Shaoyang had been installed, upper and lower were divided in discord; he requested transfer to Shouzhou to win him over by imperial command and use alienation to shake his faction; it happened that Wang Chengzong was being attacked and this was not used in time.
translations.idiomatic: While Jifu was in Huainan he heard that Wu Shaoyang had succeeded and the command was divided; he volunteered to move to Shouzhou to win him over by imperial authority and sow discord in his camp, but the campaign against Wang Chengzong intervened before the plan could be used.

sentences.zh: 後田弘正以魏歸，吉甫知魏人謂田進誠才，而唐州乃蔡喉衿，請拔進誠為刺史，以臨賊境，且慰魏心。

translations.literal: Later when Tian Hongzheng returned Wei to allegiance, Jifu knew the Wei people said Tian Jincheng had talent, while Tangzhou was Cai's throat and collar; he requested promoting Jincheng as prefect to face the rebel border and also comfort Wei hearts.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Hongzheng brought Wei back to allegiance, Jifu knew the Wei troops admired Tian Jincheng and that Tangzhou was the throat of Cai territory; he urged appointing Jincheng prefect there to press the rebels and reassure Wei.

sentences.zh: 烏重胤守河陽，吉甫以汝州捍蔽東都，聯唐、許，當蔡西面，兵寡不足憚寇，而河陽乃魏博之津，弘正歸國，則為內鎮，不宜戍重兵示不信，請徙屯汝州。

translations.literal: Wu Chongyin held Heyang; Jifu held that Ruzhou shielded the eastern capital, linked Tang and Xu, faced Cai's west, had few troops insufficient to awe rebels; yet Heyang was Weibo's ford—when Hongzheng returned to the state it became an inner command and should not garrison heavy troops showing distrust; he requested moving the garrison to Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chongyin held Heyang; Jifu argued that Ruzhou shielded the eastern capital, linked Tang and Xu, and faced Cai on the west with too few troops to overawe rebels, while Heyang was Weibo's strategic crossing—now that Hongzheng had submitted, a heavy garrison there would signal distrust; he urged transferring the troops to Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝皆從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed all of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved all these proposals.

sentences.zh: 後弘正拜檢校尚書右僕射，賜其軍錢二千萬，弘正曰：「吾未喜於移河陽軍也。

translations.literal: Later Hongzheng was appointed acting right vice director of the Secretariat and granted twenty million in cash for his army; Hongzheng said: "I am not pleased about moving the Heyang army."
translations.idiomatic: Later Hongzheng was made acting right vice director of the Secretariat and granted twenty million cash for his army; Hongzheng said, "What pleases me is not the money but moving the Heyang garrison."

sentences.zh: 」及元濟擅立，吉甫以內地無唇齒援，因時可取，不當用河朔故事，與帝意合。

translations.literal: " When Yuanji presumptuously established himself, Jifu held that the inner lands had no neighboring support like lips and teeth, and could be taken by the timely moment; the Hebei-Shanxi precedent should not be used—this matched the emperor's mind.
translations.idiomatic: " When Wu Yuanji seized power unlawfully, Jifu argued that the interior provinces lacked mutual support and could be taken now—that the old indulgence shown Hebei should not apply—and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 又請自往招元濟，茍逆誌不悛，得指授群帥俘賊以獻天子。

translations.literal: He again requested to go himself to win over Yuanji; if the rebel's will did not repent, he could direct and assign the various commanders to capture the bandit and present him to the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He again volunteered to go in person to win Yuanji over, or, if the rebel would not submit, to direct the commanders to capture him for the throne.

sentences.zh: 不許，固請至流涕，帝慰勉之。

translations.literal: It was not permitted; he firmly requested until tears flowed; the emperor comforted and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused, but Jifu pleaded until he wept; the emperor comforted him.

sentences.zh: 會暴疾卒，年五十七。

translations.literal: He then suddenly fell ill and died at fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He then died suddenly of illness at fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 帝震悼，賻外別賜縑五百恤其家，自大斂至卒哭，皆中人臨吊。

translations.literal: The emperor was shocked and grieved; beyond funeral gifts he separately bestowed five hundred bolts of silk to comfort his family; from the great encoffinment to the end of mourning wailing, eunuchs all came to condole.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was stricken with grief; beyond the usual funeral gifts he granted five hundred bolts of silk to the family, and eunuchs attended every rite from encoffinment to the end of mourning.

sentences.zh: 吉甫圖淮西地，未及上，帝敕其子獻之。

translations.literal: Jifu had mapped Huaixi territory but had not yet submitted it; the emperor ordered his son to present it.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu had drawn a map of Huaixi but died before presenting it; the emperor ordered his son to submit it.

sentences.zh: 及葬，祭以少牢，贈司空。

translations.literal: At burial he was sacrificed to with the lesser tethered victims and posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: At his burial he was honored with the lesser sacrificial rites and posthumously made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 有司謚曰敬憲，度支郎中張仲方非之，帝怒，貶仲方，更賜謚曰忠懿。

translations.literal: The relevant offices gave the posthumous title Reverent and Discerning; Revenue Bureau director Zhang Zhongfang objected; the emperor was angry and demoted Zhongfang, changing the granted title to Loyal and Excellent.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries proposed the posthumous title Reverent and Discerning; Zhang Zhongfang of the Revenue Bureau objected; the emperor, angered, demoted Zhongfang and changed the title to Loyal and Excellent.

sentences.zh: 始，吉甫當國，經綜政事，眾職咸治。

translations.literal: At first when Jifu held the state he coordinated government affairs and all duties were well governed.
translations.idiomatic: When Jifu first held power he coordinated affairs so that every office functioned well.

sentences.zh: 引薦賢士大夫，愛善無遺，褒忠臣後，以起義烈。

translations.literal: He introduced and recommended worthy scholar-officials, loving goodness without omission, praising loyal ministers' descendants to rouse righteous fervor.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted worthy scholars, cherished merit without reserve, and honored the descendants of loyal ministers to inspire public virtue.

sentences.zh: 與武元衡連位，未幾節度劍南，屢言元衡材，宜還為相。

translations.literal: He served in succession with Wu Yuanheng; before long Yuanheng was military commissioner of Jiannan; [Jifu] repeatedly said Yuanheng had talent and should return as chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: He served alongside Wu Yuanheng; when Yuanheng was posted to Jiannan as military commissioner, Jifu repeatedly urged that his talent deserved recall to the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 及再輔政，天下想望風采，而稍修怨，罷李藩宰相，而裴垍左遷，皆其謀也。

translations.literal: When he again assisted government the realm looked up to his bearing; yet he gradually nursed resentments—dismissing Li Fan as chancellor and demoting Pei Ji to a distant post were all his schemes.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to power the realm looked to him with hope, yet he also settled old scores—Li Fan's dismissal and Pei Ji's exile were his doing.

sentences.zh: 李正辭晚相失，及與蕭俛同召為翰林學士，獨用俛而罷正辭，人莫不疑憚。

translations.literal: He fell out with Li Zhengchen late; when Xiao Mian was summoned together as Hanlin academician he used only Mian and dismissed Zhengchen—none did not suspect and fear.
translations.idiomatic: He had a late falling-out with Li Zhengchen; when Xiao Mian was summoned to the Hanlin with him, Jifu kept Xiao and removed Li—no one failed to see the grudge behind it.

sentences.zh: 帝亦知其專，乃進李絳，遂與有隙，數辯爭殿上，帝多直絳。

translations.literal: The emperor also knew his arbitrariness and therefore advanced Li Jiang; thereafter they had a rift and repeatedly argued in the hall; the emperor mostly sided with Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew his dominance and advanced Li Jiang to balance him; they quarreled repeatedly in audience, and the emperor usually sided with Li.

sentences.zh: 然畏慎奉法，不忮害，顧大體。

translations.literal: Yet he was cautious in reverence, observed law, did not harm through envy, and looked to the larger pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was cautious, law-abiding, free of petty malice, and mindful of the larger interest.

sentences.zh: 左拾遺楊歸厚嘗請對，日已旰，帝令它日見，固請不肯退。

translations.literal: Left remembrancer Yang Guihou once requested audience; the day was already late; the emperor ordered to see him another day; he firmly requested and would not withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Left remembrancer Yang Guihou once sought audience after the hour had grown late; told to return another day, he refused to leave.

sentences.zh: 既見，極論中人許遂振之奸，又歷詆輔相，求自試，又表假郵置院具婚禮。

translations.literal: Once he saw the emperor he exhaustively discussed the eunuch Xu Suizhen's treachery, also repeatedly denounced the chancellors, sought to test himself, and also memorialized to borrow the courier station compound to prepare wedding rites.
translations.idiomatic: When received he denounced the eunuch Xu Suizhen at length, attacked the chancellors, demanded a trial appointment, and petitioned to borrow the courier station for his wedding.

sentences.zh: 帝怒其輕肆，欲遠斥之，李絳為言，不能得。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry at his levity and wanted to banish him far; Li Jiang spoke for him but could not obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, angered by his insolence, meant to banish him; Li Jiang spoke for him in vain.

sentences.zh: 吉甫見帝，謝引用之非，帝意釋，得以國子主簿分司東都。

translations.literal: Jifu saw the emperor and apologized for the error of recommending him; the emperor's mind was released, and [Yang] was able to become National University registrar with detached service at the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu apologized to the emperor for having recommended Yang; the emperor relented, and Yang was made registrar of the National University with detached service in the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 初，政事堂會食，有巨床，相傳徙者宰相輒罷，不敢遷，吉甫笑曰：「世俗禁忌，何足疑邪？

translations.literal: At first when the Administrative Hall dined together there was a huge couch; tradition held that whichever chancellor moved it would be dismissed, and none dared shift it; Jifu laughed and said: "Worldly taboos—what is worth doubting?"
translations.idiomatic: When the Administrative Hall dined together there was a huge couch that tradition said would cost any chancellor his office if moved; none dared touch it; Jifu laughed and said, "What are worldly superstitions to a statesman?"

sentences.zh: 」徹而新之。

translations.literal: " He removed it and made it new.
translations.idiomatic: " He had it removed and replaced with a new one.

sentences.zh: 吉甫居安邑裏，時號「安邑李丞相」。

translations.literal: Jifu dwelt in Anyi Lane and was at the time called "Chancellor Li of Anyi."
translations.idiomatic: Jifu lived in Anyi Lane and was known as "Chancellor Li of Anyi."

sentences.zh: 所論著甚多，皆行於世。

translations.literal: His treatises and writings were many and all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote extensively, and his works circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 前卒一歲，熒惑掩太微上相，吉甫曰：「天且殺我。

translations.literal: One year before his death Mars occulted the Grand Forbidden's upper chancellor star; Jifu said: "Heaven is about to kill me."
translations.idiomatic: A year before he died, Mars occulted the chancellor star in the Grand Forbidden Palace; Jifu said, "Heaven is about to take my life."

sentences.zh: 」再遜位，不許。

translations.literal: " He twice yielded his post; it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: " He twice offered to resign; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 子德修，亦有誌操，寶歷中為膳部員外郎。

translations.literal: His son Dexiu also had resolve and integrity; in the Baoli era he was vice director of the Board of Foodstuffs.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dexiu shared his moral resolve and served as vice director of the Board of Foodstuffs under Emperor Jingzong.

sentences.zh: 張仲方入為諫議大夫，德修不欲同朝，出為舒、湖、楚三州刺史。

translations.literal: When Zhang Zhongfang entered as remonstrance grandee, Dexiu did not wish to serve in the same court and went out as prefect of the three prefectures Shu, Hu, and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Zhongfang became remonstrance grandee, Dexiu declined to serve alongside him and took posts as prefect of Shu, Hu, and Chu.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 次子德裕，自有傳。

translations.literal: The second son Deyu has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Li Deyu has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 李鄘，字建侯，北海太守邕之從孫。

translations.literal: Li Yong, courtesy name Jianhou, was a grandnephew of Li Yong, prefect of Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yong, courtesy name Jianhou, was a grandnephew of the famous Li Yong, prefect of Beihai.

sentences.zh: 第進士，又以書判高等補秘書省正字。

translations.literal: He placed in the jinshi examination and, through high rank in document judgment, was supplemented as collator of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and, ranking high in the document-judgment test, was appointed collator in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 李懷光辟致幕府，擢累監察御史。

translations.literal: Li Huai'guang recruited him to his staff office; he was promoted in succession to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huai'guang brought him onto his staff, and he rose to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 懷光反河中，鄘與母、妻陷焉，因紿懷光以兄病臥洛且革，母欲往視；

translations.literal: When Huai'guang rebelled in Hezhong, Yong and his mother and wife were trapped there; he therefore deceived Huai'guang, saying his elder brother lay ill in Luoyang and was near death, and his mother wished to go see him;
translations.idiomatic: When Huai'guang rebelled in Hezhong, Yong, his mother, and his wife were trapped with him; he deceived Huai'guang by saying his elder brother lay gravely ill in Luoyang and his mother wished to visit him;

sentences.zh: 懷光許可，戒妻子無偕行。

translations.literal: Huai'guang permitted it and warned that wife and children must not go together.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang consented but forbade his wife and children to accompany her.

sentences.zh: 鄘私遣之，懷光怒，欲加罪，謝曰：「鄘籍在軍，不得為母駕，奈何不使婦往？

translations.literal: Yong secretly sent them; Huai'guang was angry and wished to punish him; Yong apologized: "Yong is registered in the army and cannot drive for his mother—how could he not send his wife?"
translations.idiomatic: Yong sent them secretly; Huai'guang was furious and meant to punish him; Yong replied, "I am bound to the army and cannot escort my mother—how could I not send my wife?"

sentences.zh: 」懷光止不問。

translations.literal: " Huai'guang stopped and did not inquire further.
translations.idiomatic: " Huai'guang let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 後與高郢刺賊虛實及所以攻取者，白諸朝，德宗手詔褒答。

translations.literal: Later, together with Gao Ying, he probed the rebels' strengths and weaknesses and how to attack and take them, reporting to the court; Dezong personally edicted praise and reply.
translations.idiomatic: Later he and Gao Ying gathered intelligence on the rebels' strengths and how to defeat them and reported to court; Dezong answered with a personal commendation.

sentences.zh: 懷光覺，嚴兵召二人問之，鄘詞氣不撓，三軍為感動，懷光不殺，囚之。

translations.literal: Huai'guang perceived it, drew up strict troops, and summoned the two to question them; Yong's tone did not bend, the three armies were moved, Huai'guang did not kill them but imprisoned them.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang discovered the leak, summoned them under arms, and interrogated them; Yong did not flinch, the army was moved, and Huai'guang imprisoned them rather than execute them.

sentences.zh: 河中平，馬燧破械致禮，表佐其府，以言不用，罷歸洛中。

translations.literal: When Hezhong was pacified, Ma Sui removed their fetters and showed courtesy, memorialized them as aides in his office; because their words were not used, they were dismissed and returned to Luoyang.
