translations.idiomatic: When Hezhong fell, Ma Sui freed them honorably and offered them posts on his staff; when their counsel went unheeded, Yong returned to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 召為吏部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was summoned as vice minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as vice minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 徐州張建封卒，兵亂，囚監軍，迫建封子愔主軍務。

translations.literal: Zhang Jianfeng of Xuzhou died; soldiers rioted, imprisoned the army supervisor, and forced Jianfeng's son Yin to manage military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jianfeng of Xuzhou died, the troops mutinied, imprisoned the army supervisor, and forced his son Yin to take command.

sentences.zh: 帝以鄘剛敢，拜宣慰使，持節直入其軍，大會士，喻以禍福，出監軍獄中，脫桎梏，使復位，眾不敢動。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Yong was firm and bold, appointed him pacification commissioner; bearing the staff he entered their army directly, held a great assembly of troops, explained fortune and disaster, brought the army supervisor out of prison, removed his fetters, restored him to position, and none dared stir.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, trusting Yong's courage, made him pacification commissioner; bearing imperial authority he entered the camp, addressed the troops on the consequences of rebellion, freed the imprisoned supervisor, and restored order without bloodshed.

sentences.zh: 愔即上表謝罪，稱兵馬留後，鄘曰：「非詔命，安得輒稱之？

translations.literal: Yin at once memorialized confessing guilt and styled himself military affairs acting commissioner; Yong said: "Without an edict, how can you presumptuously style yourself so?"
translations.idiomatic: Yin memorialized in apology and styled himself acting military commissioner; Yong said, "Without an imperial order, how dare you assume that title?"

sentences.zh: 」削去乃受。

translations.literal: " It was struck out and only then accepted.
translations.idiomatic: " Only after the title was struck out did Yong accept the memorial.

sentences.zh: 既還，稱旨，遷郎中。

translations.literal: Once he returned he matched the emperor's intent and was transferred to director.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he pleased the emperor and was promoted to director.

sentences.zh: 順宗時，進御史中丞。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Shunzong he was advanced to censor vice director.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shunzong he became vice director of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 憲宗立，為京兆尹，進尚書右丞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong ascended he became Jingzhao intendant and was advanced to right vice director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzong took the throne Yong became intendant of Jingzhao and then right vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 元和初，京師多盜賊，復拜京兆。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe the capital had many bandits and thieves; he was again appointed Jingzhao intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanhe, with banditry rife in the capital, he was again appointed Jingzhao intendant.

sentences.zh: 以檢校禮部尚書為鳳翔、隴右節度使。

translations.literal: With acting minister of Rites he became military commissioner of Fengxiang and Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made acting minister of Rites and military commissioner of Fengxiang and Longyou.

sentences.zh: 是鎮常兼神策行營，前此用武將，始受詔，即詣軍脩謁。

translations.literal: This command habitually also held the Shence campaign camp; before this military generals were used; as soon as he received the edict he went to the army to pay respects.
translations.idiomatic: That post had usually been held by generals and included command of the Shence campaign camp; on receiving his commission Yong went at once to pay his respects to the troops.

sentences.zh: 鄘以為不可，詔為去神策行營號。

translations.literal: Yong held this impossible; an edict removed the Shence campaign camp title.
translations.idiomatic: Yong objected, and the throne removed the Shence campaign designation from his commission.

sentences.zh: 俄徙河東，入為刑部尚書、諸道鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: Before long he was moved to Hedong; he entered court as minister of Justice and transport commissioner for salt and iron of all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Hedong, then recalled as minister of Justice and commissioner for salt and iron transport on all circuits.

sentences.zh: 拜淮南節度使。

translations.literal: He was appointed military commissioner of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed military commissioner of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 王師討蔡方急，李師道謀撓沮之，鄘以兵二萬分壁鄆境，貲餉不仰有司。

translations.literal: The imperial army was urgently attacking Cai; Li Shidao plotted to thwart and obstruct it; Yong stationed twenty thousand troops along the Yan border, supplies and pay not relying on the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: While imperial forces pressed the campaign against Cai, Li Shidao sought to interfere; Yong posted twenty thousand men on the Yan border at his own expense, without drawing on the central ministries.

sentences.zh: 是時兵興，天子憂財乏，使程异馳驛江淮，諷諸道輸貨助軍。

translations.literal: At that time warfare arose; the Son of Heaven worried over lack of funds and sent Cheng Yi by post-haste relay through Jianghuai to hint to the circuits to submit goods to aid the army.
translations.idiomatic: With war underway the emperor feared a shortage of funds and sent Cheng Yi post-haste through Jianghuai to urge the circuits to contribute supplies.

sentences.zh: 鄘素富強，即籍府庫留一歲儲，餘盡納於朝，諸道由是悉索以獻，繄鄘倡之。

translations.literal: Yong had always been wealthy and strong; he at once registered the treasury, kept one year's stores, and submitted the rest entirely to the court; the circuits thereupon all searched out and presented—this was initiated by Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Yong's circuit was prosperous; he inventoried the treasury, kept one year's reserves, and sent the rest to the capital—whereupon other circuits followed his example.

sentences.zh: 先是，吐突承璀為監軍，貴寵甚，鄘以剛嚴治，相禮憚，稍厚善。

translations.literal: Earlier Tutu Chenghuan was army supervisor, greatly favored and petted; Yong governed with stern severity; they mutually showed ritual and fear, and gradually grew rather cordial.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the eunuch Tutu Chenghuan had been army supervisor and enjoyed great favor; Yong governed sternly; mutual respect grew into a workable rapport.

sentences.zh: 承璀歸，數稱薦之，召拜門下侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: When Chenghuan returned he repeatedly praised and recommended him; he was summoned and appointed vice director of the Chancellery and associate director of the Secretariat Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: When Chenghuan returned to court he recommended Yong repeatedly; Yong was summoned as vice director of the Chancellery and chancellor.

sentences.zh: 鄘不喜由宦幸進，及出祖，樂作泣下，謂諸將曰：「吾老安外鎮，宰相豈吾任乎？

translations.literal: Yong disliked advancement through eunuch favor; when he went out to the farewell feast, as the music played he wept and said to the generals: "I am old and content in an outer command—how is chancellor my post?"
translations.idiomatic: Yong disliked advancement through eunuch patronage; at his farewell feast he wept as the music played and told his officers, "I am old and content in the provinces—what have I to do with the chancellorship?"

sentences.zh: 」至京師，不肯視事，引疾固辭，改戶部尚書。

translations.literal: " On reaching the capital he refused to handle affairs, cited illness and firmly declined, and was changed to minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: " In the capital he refused to take up office, pleaded illness, and was reassigned as minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 俄檢校尚書左僕射，兼太子賓客，分司東都。

translations.literal: Before long he was acting left vice director of the Secretariat, concurrently crown prince guest, with detached service at the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became acting left vice director of the Secretariat and crown prince guest with detached service in the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 以太子少傅致仕，卒，贈太子太保，謚曰肅。

translations.literal: He retired as crown prince junior tutor, died, was posthumously made crown prince grand guardian, and given the posthumous title Solemn.
translations.idiomatic: He retired as junior tutor to the crown prince, died, was posthumously honored as grand guardian of the crown prince, and given the posthumous title Solemn.

sentences.zh: 鄘強直無私，與楊憑、穆質、許孟容、王仲舒友善，皆以氣自任。

translations.literal: Yong was forceful, upright, and without selfishness; he was friendly with Yang Ping, Mu Zhi, Xu Mengrong, and Wang Zhongshu, all taking spirit as their charge.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was upright and selfless, friendly with Yang Ping, Mu Zhi, Xu Mengrong, and Wang Zhongshu—men who prided themselves on moral courage.

sentences.zh: 而鄘當官，以峭法操下，所至稱治。

translations.literal: When Yong held office he used stern law to control subordinates; wherever he went was called well governed.
translations.idiomatic: In office he ruled subordinates with stern law and was praised for good governance wherever he served.

sentences.zh: 猛決少恩，在淮南七年，其生殺禽擿，多委軍吏，而參佐束手不得與，人往往陷非法，議者亦以此少之。

translations.literal: Fierce in decision and sparing in grace, during seven years in Huainan his executions, captures, and arrests were mostly entrusted to army clerks, while aides stood by with hands bound unable to participate; people often fell into unlawful acts, and critics for this reason also slighted him.
translations.idiomatic: He was fierce and sparing of mercy; during seven years in Huainan he left life-and-death decisions largely to military staff while his civil aides stood idle; many suffered injustice, and critics held this against him.

sentences.zh: 子拭，仕歷宗正卿、京兆尹、河東鳳翔節度使，以秘書監卒。

translations.literal: His son Shi served as director of the Imperial Clan Court, Jingzhao intendant, and military commissioner of Hedong and Fengxiang, and died as director of the Secretariat Library.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shi rose through the posts of director of the Imperial Clan Court, Jingzhao intendant, and commissioner of Hedong and Fengxiang, and died as director of the Secretariat Library.

sentences.zh: 拭子磎，字景望。

translations.literal: Shi's son Xi, courtesy name Jingwang.
translations.idiomatic: Shi's son was Li Xi, courtesy name Jingwang.

sentences.zh: 大中末，擢進士，累遷戶部郎中，分司東都。

translations.literal: At the end of Dazhong he was selected as jinshi and promoted in succession to director of the Revenue Bureau with detached service at the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Dazhong era he passed the jinshi and rose to director of the Revenue Bureau with detached service in the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 劾奏內園使郝景全不法事，景全反摘磎奏犯順宗嫌名，坐奪俸。

translations.literal: He impeached Inner Garden commissioner Hao Jingquan for unlawful acts; Jingquan in turn seized on Xi's memorial for violating Emperor Shunzong's taboo name, and he was punished by salary confiscation.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Inner Garden commissioner Hao Jingquan for misconduct; Jingquan retaliated by accusing Xi's memorial of violating Shunzong's taboo name, and Xi was fined by salary confiscation.

sentences.zh: 磎上言：「『因事告事，旁訟他人』者，咸通詔語也。

translations.literal: Xi submitted: "'Reporting an affair by means of an affair, litigating against others on the side'—this is language from a Xiantong edict."
translations.idiomatic: Xi memorialized, "The phrase 'using one case to report another, dragging in unrelated parties' comes from a Xiantong edict."

sentences.zh: 禮，不諱嫌名；

translations.literal: In ritual, taboo homophones are not avoided;
translations.idiomatic: According to ritual, taboo homophones need not be avoided;

sentences.zh: 律，廟諱嫌名不坐。

translations.literal: in law, temple-taboo homophones are not punished.
translations.idiomatic: and by law, offenses involving temple-taboo homophones are not punishable.

sentences.zh: 豈臣所引詔書而有司輒論奏？

translations.literal: How can the edict I cited be judged and memorialized by the relevant offices?
translations.idiomatic: How can the ministries punish me for quoting an edict?

sentences.zh: 臣恐自今用格令者，委曲回避，旁緣為奸也。

translations.literal: Your servant fears that from now those who use regulations will evade circuitously and attach to side matters to commit treachery.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that hereafter anyone citing regulations will be forced into evasive circumlocution, opening the door to abuse.

sentences.zh: 」詔不奪俸。

translations.literal: " An edict did not confiscate salary.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor ordered his salary restored.

sentences.zh: 黃巢陷洛，磎挾尚書八印走河陽，時留守劉允章為賊脅，遣人就磎索印，拒不與。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao took Luoyang, Xi carried off the eight seals of the Secretariat and fled to Heyang; at the time the acting commander Liu Yunzhang was coerced by the bandits and sent someone to Xi to demand the seals; he refused to give them.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao seized Luoyang, Xi fled to Heyang with the eight seals of the Secretariat; the acting commander Liu Yunzhang, pressured by the rebels, sent men to demand them, but Xi refused.

sentences.zh: 允章悟，亦不臣賊。

translations.literal: Yunzhang came to awareness and also did not submit to the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzhang took heart and likewise refused to serve the rebels.

sentences.zh: 嗣襄王之亂，轉側淮南，高駢受偽命，磎苦諫，不納。

translations.literal: During the turmoil of the succession of the Prince of Xiang, he shifted about in Huainan; Gao Pian accepted a false commission; Xi remonstrated bitterly and was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: During the succession crisis of the Prince of Xiang he moved about in Huainan; Gao Pian accepted a false imperial commission, and Xi's earnest remonstrance went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 入為中書舍人、翰林學士。

translations.literal: He entered as Secretariat drafter and Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Secretariat drafter and Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 辭職歸華陰，復以學士召。

translations.literal: He resigned his post and returned to Huayin; he was again summoned as academician.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned and retired to Huayin, then was summoned back to the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 磎好學，家有書至萬卷，世號「李書樓」。

translations.literal: Xi loved learning; his household had books reaching ten thousand scrolls, and the age called him "Li the Book Tower."
translations.idiomatic: Xi was a devoted scholar; his household held ten thousand scrolls, and he was known as "Li the Book Tower."

sentences.zh: 所著文章及註解諸書傳甚多。

translations.literal: His composed essays and commentaries on various classics and histories were many.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote extensively, including many commentaries on the classics.

sentences.zh: 子沇，字東濟，有俊才，亦遇害，贈禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: His son Yan, courtesy name Dongji, had outstanding talent, also met with violent death, and was posthumously made vice director of the Board of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yan, courtesy name Dongji, was a gifted man who also died violently and was posthumously honored as vice director of the Board of Rites.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：剛者天德，故孔子稱「剛近仁」。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Firmness is Heaven's virtue; therefore Confucius said "firmness is near to humaneness."
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal says: Firmness is Heaven's virtue; hence Confucius said that firmness borders on humaneness.

sentences.zh: 骨強四支，故君有忠臣，謂之骨鯁。

translations.literal: Bones strengthen the four limbs; therefore when a lord has loyal ministers they are called bone spines.
translations.idiomatic: Strong bones support the limbs; so loyal ministers who speak blunt truth are called the backbone of the state.

sentences.zh: 若棲筠、庸阝二子，其剛者歟！

translations.literal: As for the two men Qiyun and Yong—are they not the firm ones!
translations.idiomatic: Of Qiyun and Yong—were these not men of true firmness!

sentences.zh: 棲筠抗權邪，不及相；

translations.literal: Qiyun resisted powerful wickedness but did not reach the chancellorship;
translations.idiomatic: Qiyun defied corrupt power yet never became chancellor;

sentences.zh: 庸阝得相，不願拜。

translations.literal: Yong obtained the chancellorship but did not wish to accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was offered the chancellorship and refused to accept it.

sentences.zh: 非剛，疇克勝之？

translations.literal: Without firmness, who could overcome such things?
translations.idiomatic: Without such firmness, who could have done what they did?

sentences.zh: 吉甫踐天宰，謀謨是矣，而鯁正有愧於父雲。

translations.literal: Jifu trod the post of Heaven's minister; his stratagems were right, yet in blunt uprightness he had shame before his father's cloud.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu held the highest office and his statecraft was sound, yet in blunt integrity he fell short of his father's example.
